HelpTopic.Name: Improved Help for Lightning App: Tree Builder

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
Help Topics are bite-sized pieces of information that can be associated with items on a user's screen or simply made available for users to read on demand, for example by browsing through hierarchies of material displayed on a 'Tree Viewer':

Use this screen to:

  • Add a new tree:
    • Open the 'Ellipsis' menu (click the three dots icon) on the Tree View.
    • Click the 'Add Tree' button then enter a name for the Topic that will become the 'root' of your new tree.
  • Set your new tree as the default for this screen:
    • Click the 'Set Default Topic' button on the ellipsis menu of the Tree and also the Topic viewer to show your new Tree as the default content when refreshing this page.
    • Click the 'Edit' button on the ellipsis menu of the Topic viewer to update your text or add media.
  • Build out your tree:
    • Use the 'Add' tools on the tree to create peer and child branch Topics.

With Improved Help:

  • Help Administrators control overall branding settings for a given Help installation:
    • Visit the 'Branding' tab of the Help Global Settings page to gain access to key system-wide settings.
    • In classic scenarios, the path to a 'customer stylesheet' can be set: this should be based on the default version that comes packaged with Help, and will be included on the majority of the Visualforce pages that form much of our classic Help UI.
    • In Lightning scenarios, styling information can be keyed directly into the settings screen and will take effect as soon as changes are saved.
  • Help Authors select from a range of preset styling options for their Help Topics:
    • Navigate to the desired Help Topic in any Lighting Topic Viewer component or the Help Portal.
    • Open the Ellipsis menu and click the Edit tool.
    • Select the 'Status' tab.
    • Select a style from the 'Custom Style' drop down.
    • Save and refresh the Topic to see changes, which will vary depending on the style chosen.

The 'Text' tab of the Help Topic editor panel includes a 'Keywords' field. Enter a word or short phrase into this box to turn the Topic being edited into the 'destination' to which any other Topic referencing the Keyword will be automatically linked.

Please note the following:

  • Links appear in the main, rich text body of Help Topics (i.e., it is the text in their Description fields into which links are inserted).
  • As of the current Help release, linking is on the basis of text containing the exact word or phrase entered as the Keyword with a space either side of it.

Install the latest release of Improved Help into your Salesforce org, using the appropriate link for your situation:

  • Log in to the desired destination Salesforce org as a System Administrator.
  • Installation hyperlinks are unique to the precise package version to which they apply. Please contact Improved Apps for the latest links.
  • Click the link and, when prompted, select one of the following installation security options:
    • Install for Admins Only: Controlled roll-out (especially in any Production Orgs)
    • Install for all Users: For product evaluation (typically in Sandbox or Development Orgs)
Here's how to get going!

Note that you must be a Salesforce System Administrator or have the Salesforce ‘Customize Application’ permission to complete the following steps.

Where possible, we recommend switching to the Lightning Experience and proceeding as follows:

  • Switch to the Improved Help for Lightning app.
  • On the 'Welcome' tab, click the 'Initialise Settings' button to create some default product settings, covering areas such as product preferences and branding.
  • Use the 'Upsert Configuration Tools' button to initialise certain Help clickables, such as menu items and tools offered on helped Lightning pages.
  • Refresh the Welcome tab to see additional help and guidance materials created as part of the initialisation steps completed above.
  • Click the tab or link to the Help Settings page to review additional global options at any time.


Where Lighting is not available:

  • Switch to the Improved Help app.
  • Click the Help Settings tab.
  • Initialise settings using the button on the 'Quick Start' tab.

At this stage, you may want to give some thought to some important implementation considerations that can impact the way you configure help and manage your content.

Key areas to bear in mind include:

  • Who will your end users be?
  • Who will be authoring the required content?
  • Do I need to provide different help to different groups of people?
  • Will this be an international / multi-lingual deployment?
  • Are there existing materials I can use as seed corn or which will need to be referenced?


Improved Apps are more than happy to discuss these with you: we're confident Improved Help can rise to these and other challenges.

Alternatiively, feel free to dive straight in to implementing Improved Help for the Salesforce environments that are relevant to your organisation.

Apply the correct Permission Set for Users as needed. They are hierarchical, so each user only needs the highest level of the following (don’t worry if you add multiple Permission Sets – Improved Help ignores all but the highest):

  • Helped Users: Can view help content & comment;
  • Help Analyst: As above but can also access Help Analysis mode to view statistics (they also need reporting permissions set at their Profile level);
  • Help Authors: As Above but can also edit help content and view Inactive Help Topics;
  • Help Administrators: As above but can also access Improved Help Setting Page. Profile-level ‘Customize Application’ rights are needed to save Help Settings changes.

A license is required to use Improved Help. License assignment is managed according to the contracted subscription level:


  • Named-User Subscriptions (including Trials): Use Installed Packages - Assign Licenses;
  • Org-wide Subscriptions: No action required.
Please refer to the Resources attached to this Topic for more information.

Improved Help can be made available in many cases to non-Salesforce web pages where:

  • Improved Help 'hooking' scripts can be added to the remote pages or
  • It is acceptable to access the sites concerned via a browser enabled with Improved Help extensions.


Please contact your Improved Apps Account Manager for more information.
The following sections describe the main steps required to deploy Improved Help across the various Salesforce environments you may wish to provision:

For each Page Layout you will need to create a new button or custom link, which will reveal embedded help for the tab:

  • Use a button if you would like embedded Help to appear only when users request it: they click the button to switch on Help if they wish to each time they refresh the tab.
  • Use a link if you want embedded Help to appear automatically for a given layout.


For full details, please see the Resources attached to this Topic.

There are many ways to add Help to your Salesforce pages. To get going, you must add a custom button or a link in the side-bar, which when clicked, shows available Improved Help available ?mark icons next to any helped elements in the page and the Quick Access Menu (top right of any page).

The simplest way to get started is to create a new 'Your 'In-App' Coach!' Home Page Help & Training Component and put it on your Home Page Layouts:

  • Create a link:
    • Go into Setup... Customise...Home...Custom Links
    • Click the 'New' button to create a new link
    • Label = 'Help on this Page!' (or whatever will work for your users)
    • Behaviour = 'Execute JavaScript'
    • Content Source = 'OnClick JavaScripts'
    • Paste the following code in the big white box below:


var scr = document.createElement('script');

scr.setAttribute('src', '/resource/iahelp__IHResources/js/jsConsole.js');

document.head.appendChild(scr);


  • Click 'Save'
  • Create a links component:
    • Go into Setup... Customise...Home...Home Page Components
    • Click the 'New' button to create a new 'Links' component
    • Call this 'Your 'In-App' Coach!' (or whatever will work for your users)
    • Add the Link you created above in step 1 of this section (Help on this Page!)
    • Click 'Save'
  • Add the links component to your page layout:
    • Go into Setup... Customise...Home...Home Page Layouts
    • Edit your desired Home Page Layout (or create a clone to test with a subset of users if testing in a Production org)
    • Add the 'Your 'In-App' Coach!' component to your side bar and place it somewhere near the top.
    • Click 'Save'.

Classic and Lightning Communities (such as 'Napili' and the latest templates) are fully supported:

  • For classic, our 'help hooking' components can be added to the shared scripts of an entire community or particular areas / pages as desired, bringing the Quick Access Menu and / or embedded help to community users.
  • For Lightning, community layouts can feature our Lightning components, much as with internally facing pages.


Please contact us for guidance on setup options for your situation and use cases.

Help ships with a number of Lightning components that can be presented to users in a number of ways:

  • On record layouts
  • On custom app pages
  • Via the Utility Bar
  • Via Lightning Out.


The sections which follow describe the features of each component and how to use them.

All that’s needed to setup Salesforce1 Improved Help is to:

  1. Go to Setup – Build – Customize – Chatter – Publisher Layouts
  2. Edit the Global Layout;
  3. Add ‘Improved Help’ Action;
  4. Save.


That’s it! Any Improved Help content you have created will now be available to your Salesforce1 users in the appropriate contexts.

For more information, please see the Resources attached to this Topic.

Improved Help enables help-enabling of any HTML tags in the helped Visual Force page. Typically pages will include Apex tags for data display and/or entry – and some of these may be placed in Apex tabular page blocks, to provide a user interface like standard classic pages.

Where tabular Apex form tags are used, Improved Help’s hooking mechanism recognises the rendered page markup and provide automated support of help callout positioning and sizing – so Improved Help behaves the same way on standard page layouts and Visual Force pages made to look & feel like standard pages.

So, the page developer has more flexibility over page layout and the way any Apex form tags are used:

  • General HTML ‘non-Apex’ tags;
  • Tabular Apex tags:
    • Apex Detail tag: A full standard page in classic tabular layout;
    • Apex Page Blocks: together with their enclosed, tabular Apex field tags;
  • Individual non-tabular Apex tags: within more free-form page designs.


Please see the Resources attached to this Topic for further information.

Configuration Items are records like any other in Salesforce, so can be imported and exported in any number of ways. Improved Help ships with a number of facilities to assist with this.

Note that our Lightning components will operate quite happily without any Configuration Items being present in the org: this simply means fewer options will be available when using them.

  • To download the tools defined in an org: click the "Download JSON" tool on the Global Settings page. This will downoad a copy of all configuration item records (with the exception of any where Skip Export has been set to True) in Javascript Object Notation (JSON) format, ready for upload into any other Helped Salesforce org.


  • To upload from a JSON file: upload the JSON file created via export as a Salesforce document, paste its "View File" url into the JSON location text box then click the "Upsert Configuration Tools" button on the Global Settings page. This will permanently erase all existing configuration item records with the exception of any where "Prevent Import Overwrites" has been set to True.


  • To initialise configuration items: leave the JSON location box at its default value (as on arrival on the Global Settings page) then click the "Upsert Configuration Tools" button. This will reset your configuration items to the values shipped with your release of Improved Help.

Action Code

The “message” raised when the configuration item is clicked. Our component framework code “understands” a certain set of these messages as at any given release. Examples of the meaning of certain of the current set of known action codes include “Log a comment” and “Show a Callout”.

The effect of this is that Orgs can control how action messages are raised (the particular clickable that raises it / its look, feel and positioning etc) but cannot dynamically add new messages (or if they do, they cannot usefully be processed as they will not be understood).

Icon Class

Defines the icon to display for a given clickable: note that only certain clickable types include icons (e.g., dropdowns do not, whereas ellipsis tools do).


The class is, in fact, the name of an icon from the set provided by “Font Awesome” (see the searchable list provided here: http://fontawesome.io/icons/ ).

Label

Defines the text displayed alongside the tool. These can be plain English text, but need to be internationalisation “codes” for multilingual environments.

Description

Descriptive text describing the purpose and functioning of the configuration tool.

Display Grouping

Not currently used

Display Order

Positions the tool in the collection within which it appears. For example, the lowest numbered drop down tool appears at the top of its drop down list.

Has Divider

For Dropdown and Ellipsis tools only, places a horizontal dividing line above the tool when set to “True”.

Icon Content

Text to overlay over the icon displayed for a tool. For example, the Add / Remove Bookmark tools use “ ” and “-” respectively, overlaid on the base bookmark icon that both use.

Permission Level

Defines which user types have access to a given tool. Options are:


  • 1 = All Helped Users

  • 2 = Analysts or above.

  • 4 = Authrs or above.

  • 8 = Administrator only.


Prevent Import Overwrites

Used to control configuration item import behaviour. As a rule when uploading configuration tools via the button on the Settings page, all existing items are deleted and overwritten by the new records. Set this flag to True on a configuration item record to prevent it from being overwritten in this way.

Negotiate Toolbar Level

Specify a positive integer to allow this item to feature in lists of tool “shortcuts”, such as those presented via the handle of Quick Access Menu components whose “Show Shortcuts” option is ticked.

Tip Text

The tool tip, internationalised as per Label.

Tool Class

Can be used to style individual tools. As an example, Tool Class is used to differentiate the appearance (colour) of the Add and Remove Bookmark tools.

Tool Context

Controls which of each type of tool appear in which of our Lightning components. For example, it is possible to have one set of Ellipsis tools on the Help Topic Viewer and a different set on the Listing component. Select from one of the following pick-list values:


  • [Hidden] - Can be used to temporarily hide a particular tool

  • Builder - Reserved for future use

  • CardHelpTopic - The Help Topic Viewer.

  • CardReadingLists - The List when Listing Type = Reading Lists

  • CardRelatedHelp - The List when Listing Type = Related Help

  • CardRelatedTags - The tagging control in Associate mode

  • CardResources - The List when Listing Type = Related Resources

  • CardStickies - The List when showing My Help Notes

  • CardTags - The tagging control in Search mode

  • CardTree - The tree viewer

  • FixedHelp - The List when Listing Type = Fixed

  • ImageViewer - The Image Viewer

  • NewSticky - Tools to show on entry to the Help Notes creation screen.

  • QAM - The Quick Access Menu

  • RLViewer - The Reading List Viewer


Note: when Diagnostics are enabled (see elsewhere in this document) clicking the text in the footer of a given card will show a message that includes the Tool Context and Action Code that were involved in the last operation performed by it.





Tool Filter

For listing tools only, controls the record types that should feature the tool, as follows:


  • -1 = Tool should appear against rows on all list types

  • 0 = N/A - configuration tool record is not of Type = Listing

  • 1 = Help Topics

  • 2 = Bookmarks

  • 4 = Reading Lists and Reading List Entries

  • 8 = Resources

  • 16 = Help Relationships

  • 32 = Search Results

  • 64 = Help Notes (“stickies”)


The numbers can be added together as required. For example, to feature a tool on lists of Help Topics or Search Results, enter 33 (1 32).

Type

Defines the positioning of the configuration tool, as per the screen-shot at the head of this table. Options are:


  • Drop-down

  • Ellipsis

  • Header

  • Listing


Note that these are pick-list values so must be entered precisely as shown. The following values are also possible but not currently in use:


  • Footer

  • Extension

Skip Export

Used to control configuration item export behaviour. As a rule when downloading configuration tools via the button on the Settings page, all items are exported to the resulting JSON text file. Set this flag to True on a configuration item record to prevent it from being downloaded. This is useful when creating tools for local use only that one does not wish to migrate between orgs.


Supporting Controls

For tools of Type = Header only, a string defining additional controls that are required to support the action implied when the tool is clicked. For example, the “Search” header tool requires an associated search text box in order to function.


For each supporting tool, the string is in the general form shown below:


ID ~ Type ~ Label ~ Placeholder text ~ Value ^


… where…


  • ID is the HTML unique ID for the supporting control;

  • Type defines the broad type of supporting control. Recognised types are:

  • Text: produces a text entry control;

  • Drop Target: produces an area that accepts drop events as part of drag and drop operations;

  • Draggable: produces an area that can be dragged as part of drag and drop operations;


  • Label is an optional text label to display to the left of the control;

  • Placeholder text is the text to show when no value is present in the control (for certain types only);

  • Value is the default value to place in the control; and

  • The capek (^) is used to separate each required supporting control.


Spaces have been added to the model for clarity: the actual string is delimited by tildes (~) and capeks only.

HelpTopic.Name: Improved Help for Lightning App: Content Upload Wizard (Beta)

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
If you have text in sources such as external web pages or documents that you wish to convert into one or more Help Topics, you can use the 'Wizard' shown on the right of the 'Content Upload Wizard' screen to streamline the process.

Click a wizard step on the 'path' towards the top of the screen, then follow the instructions on each wizard step to:

  • Capture:
    • Type, copy or drag some or all of your source text to the input area on the left of the wizard step.
    • Select some of this text then click the " " icon to turn it into a draft Topic.
    • Repeat to create as many candidate Topics as you wish.
  • Define:
    • Your draft topics are 'listed' by selector lozenges towards the top of this step.
    • Select a draft, then use the icons in the middle of the step screen to set Topic Name, Summary and full Description texts.
  • Review:
    • Save the Topics produced in the previous steps: Please note: you must do this before attempting to place Topics on the Tree.
    • Use the 'Tree' tool against a Topic of your choice to set it to be the 'root' of the tree control on the right of the wizard step.
    • With a root set, position your remaining Topics onto the 'Tree' fby dragging and dropping.
Use this app to perform common authoring and maintenance tasks.

HelpTopic.Name: Improved Help for Lightning App: Tagging

HelpTopics.HelpTopic:
The Improved Help 'Tags' component makes it possible to 'tag' Help Topics with metadata (by relating them to other, tag Topics). Tags and the tagging component can be used to:

  • Mark Topics with attributes of interest, for example:
    • Create a 'Priority' pool, with tags for 'Urgent', 'High', 'Medium' and 'Low' learning priority content;
    • Use a 'Confidentiality' pool to advise users of the sensitivity of the content in particular Topics, with member tags such as 'Internal Use Only' or 'Public';
    • Mark content as it develops with the tags in a 'Quality' pool, which might have members such as 'Draft' or 'Approved';
    • Help users locate the Topics most relevant to their role by producing a pool with tags representing job functions or departments, then marking training materials accordingly.
  • Search and / or scope listings by reference to membership of a pool or possession of a tag.
  • Present 'Nudges' to users using the Nudge component, which displays a randomised Topic from a specified pool on arrival on a page.


To get going:

  • Search for or create a Topic to include in a pool.
  • Use the 'Add New Pool' tool in the ellipsis menu of the tagging component to produce a new pool.
  • Add further member tags representing attributes applicable to the pool by dragging topics from the list or topic viewer.

The Salesforce Lightning Experience is fundamentally less 'monolithic' than Classic: whereas the latter is quite fixed in terms of page layout, Lightning allows great flexibility in terms of how pages are laid out and which facilities (components) they contain.

Improved Help comes complete with a large number of packaged components that can be added anywhere Salesforce allows vendors to do this (which is most places!) Each of these components provides comprehensive configuration options, giving great flexibility and power in precisely how help is made available to users in different scenarios. The components are designed to be able to ‘talk’ to each other to drive dynamic content, driven by context or user interactions.

In general, a 'page owner' (usually a system administrator) edits Lighting page layouts to include the components they desire:

  1. Lightning page owner selects a component from those available...
  2. ... drags it into position where desired on their layout...
  3. ... then sets component properties.

Help Vote Sets allow Authors to give users the ability to cast a vote on a particular piece of content or record their opinions on important business issues. For example, one might want to ask Users to rate a particular Help Topic or to choose from options regarding organisational priorities in a particular area.

Click the maintenance link on the Status tab of the Help Topic Editor to see the Vote Sets defined within your Org.

How it works
  • The Help Vote Set represents the question that Users are to be asked.
  • For each Vote Set, Authors define Help Vote Options representing the answers Users can select (i.e., the votes they can cast).
  • When Users cast their votes, these are recorded as Help Interactions: Administrators and Help Analysts are able to monitor and report on these Interactions.
  • Votes are always related to a particular Help Topic, details of which are recorded with the Help Interaction.
  • Users may change their minds at any time and vote as many times as they wish. All votes are retained.
  • As soon as a Help Vote Set is selected for a Topic and changes saved, voting becomes available throughout Improved Help for the Topic in question, including:
    • In Help Callouts;
    • In the 'classic' Help Portal;
    • In Salesforce1;
    • In the Guide and Reading List viewers.
Help Vote Sets
Enter the following information to define a Vote Set:
  • Name: A reference name for the Vote Set. Users do not see this name.
  • Question Text: (Optional) The text of a question to ask Users when presenting available votes.
  • Image: The full or relative HTML path to an image to present to the user when presenting the Vote Set. This should be a small icon-like image, as it will be presented at 16 pixels high.
Help Vote Options
Enter the following information for each Vote Option (available answer) to offer as part of the Vote Set:
  • Name: A reference name for the Vote Option. Users do not see this name.
  • Option Label: (Optional) The text of answer for which users can vote in response to the question posed.
  • Image: The full or relative HTML path to an image to present to the user when presenting the Vote Option. This should be a small icon-like image, as it will be presented at 16 pixels high.
  • Display Order: Defines the order in which to display the Vote Options presented as part of the Vote Set.
Vote Sets can include a textual question and / or an image. Please click the Vote Sets link to maintain these.
Vote Sets can include a textual question and / or an image. Please click the Vote Sets link to maintain these.
Help Topic Name features in all Full Topic Templates and is used as the label text for search results and Reading List Entry names.
Help Topic Summary is displayed in most Callout Templates, as well as all Full Topic Templates. It is also used as tip text in certain cases.

Callouts are the means of displaying Improved Help embedded within a User's Salesforce or Visualforce pages. Authors can choose from one of several Callout Templates that control how much Topic information is displayed and the precise format used.
Selecting a Callout Template will automatically set a suitable default value for this field but Authors are free to amend Callout Height as they see fit.

Callouts that incude rich media generally feature Topic image or video but not both: this field specifies which media is to be used for this Topic. Note that if the selected media is not available but the alternative is, Improved Help will revert to using the available media.

"Topic Details" and "Reading Lists" are examples of Callout Templates that feature media.

This field has no impact on Callouts that do not feature media, such as "Summary Only" and does not affect the presentation of the Topic in its Full Template.
Be aware that even where "Read More" links are disabled for a particular Topic, Users may still see it in its Full Template (in the Help Portal) by searching for it.
This value is particularly useful in cases where limited screen real estate is available and Orgs wish to ensure that Users will see all related lists without scrolling being required.
Only Help Topics that are marked as "Active" can be seen by Helped Users: non-active Topics are hidden from Guides, Reading Lists and search results.

Where "Read More" is enabled, a Callout will feature a link to view the full Topic in the Help Portal. Authors can choose to disable this feature if it is felt that sufficient information can be made available via the Callout, avoiding the need to leave the working page.

Help Topics always include links to related help where Authors have chosen to define these relationships. Global Settings can be used to control whether or not to include Related Help listings for Topics from which the current Topic is referenced.

This check box can be used to override Global Settings, ensuring that any referring Topics are always shown for the current Topic.
The Status field is not used by Improved Help itself, but Organisations may choose to use it for general categorisation purposes or as part of a workflow.

The Visibility field is not used by Improved Help itself, but Organisations can choose to create data sharing rules based on the setting of the Visibility field to filter the records seen by different groups of Users.

The Custom Style field can be used to finesse the appearance of individual Help Topics. To use this field:

  • Help Administrators must define custom styles in the Customer CSS file.
  • Help Administrators then reference these styles on the Branding tab of the Global Settings page.
  • Authors are then able to select from the list of custom styles for their Topics.


Custom Styles are applied to Callout and Full Topic Templates.

Modes are as follows:

  • Local: Step is shown in the Guide Window only.
  • Automatic: Step will be shown immediately as the user clicks it in the Guide Window.
  • Manual: First Manual step in a "set" will be shown immediately, but each subsequent Manual Step will require action from the User to trigger it.
Use the Layout selector tool to specify the Helped Page Layout that will feature in this Guide Step.
Select a Helped Element that features on the selected Step Layout.

Step Context should be set to one of the following value types:

  • Enter the full ID of a Salesforce object record to feature that precise record in the Guide Step.
  • Use [Object 3 letter code]/o to show a record selection screen for that object, for example 001/o if you wish the user to use this step to select an Account.
  • Use [Object 3 letter code]/e to add a new record, for example 001/e to add a new Account.
  • Leave blank to have this Step adopt the "context" of a record selected in a previous step.
  • Use /e to enter record editing mode on a record selected in a previous step.

Guide Steps always feature a Guide "Prompt" that offers tools to allow the User to navigate the Guide where relevant. Check this box to additionally show the Help Callout for the Helped Element featuring in the Guide Step.

Setting a Salesforce Help URL causes an additional icon to appear in the Help Portal toolbar for the Topic in question. Clicking the icon takes the User to the selected URL (which need not, in fact, be from the Salesforce Help system).
This brief Reading List is one of a series designed to show Help Authors how to make the best use of each of the fields presented on the Help Portal's Topic editor panel.

Data Driven Help is a feature of Improved Help that allows you to control the help that Users see based on the Salesforce record they are viewing. For example, you may wish to show different Help Topics depending on the Stage an Opportunity has reached or the Actual Cost of a Campaign.

This feature works by allowing Authors to create multiple Helped Element records for a given on-screen "helpable" (button, field, custom link etc) each with differing "Data-driven filter" values. Improved Help selects the Helped Element to use (and thus the associated Help Topic to display) by comparing these filters with the record the User is viewing; if the data does not "pass" the filtering criteria, it is not made available to the User.

Authors should strive to observe the following guidelines when using Data Driven Help:
  • Filters should be mutually exclusive, such that only 1 Helped Element is available at any given time.
  • If any Helped Element record for a given helpable has a data driven filter, all its Helped Elements should do so. This is because:
  • If more than 1 Element record's filter matches the record being viewed, the one that will actually be used cannot be specified and:
  • Blank data driven filters mean "all records pass" - essentially ensuring that the Element is unfiltered. This is the default for new Helped Elements.

Given the above, one should also bear in mind that Helped Elements for items shown on non-record pages (e.g., list views) should not make use of data driven help.

To use Data Driven Help:
  • Help-enable the relevent Element in the usual way, then return to View mode.
  • From the Quick Access Menu, select "Re-configure" mode.
  • Select the newly enabled Element to see its "Improved Help Element Maintenance" dialogue.
  • Use the editing controls to add and amend Element records as required, pointing each at the desired Help Topics.
  • For each Element, set the "Data-driven filter" field to a suitable value, as described elsewhere in this Reading List.

Data driven filters take the following general form:

[Field name] [Operator] [Delimiter] [Value] [Delimiter]

[Field name] is the API name for the field by which you wish to filter.

Note that:
  • These are case sensitive.
  • The API name is often NOT the same as the on-screen label. To find the API name:
    • For standard objects, goto Setup | Customize | {the required object} | Fields: see the value in the "Field Name" column.
    • For custom objects, goto Setup | Create | Objects | {the required object}: find the field and see the "Field Name" or "API Name" column.

As a general rule:
  • Field names do not allow spaces.
  • Custom field names have "__c" appended to them.

[Operator] is one of the following comparison operators:

=Equals
<>Does not equal
>Greater than
<Less than
>=Greater than or equal to
<=Less than or equal to
LIKESimilar to - for use in text comparisons only. Use the "%" character as a "wildcard" when using LIKE, for example:

Type LIKE 'Exist%'

... could be used to match "Existing Customer - Upgrade" or "Existing Customer - Downgrade".

[Delimiter] is a suitable delimiting character to surround the value being sought in the filter, as follows:

  • For text (includes all pick list values), use single quotation marks (').
  • For numeric values and dates/date times, use no delimiter character.
  • For boolean values (e.g., the value of a check box), use no delimiter character.

[Value] is the value sought.

Note that:
  • For checkboxes, this will be "true" for checked or "false" for not checked (quotes here for clarity - do not use in the filter).
  • Dates should be in the form: YYYY-MM-DD
  • For date/times, use: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.
    • Times are expressed in Universal Time (UTC) also known as "Z"ulu time, so 8.15am on 3rd January 2014 San Francisco time would be rendered as: 2014-01-03T16:15:00Z

Data driven filters can be based on multiple values in one or more fields by adding criteria together. To do this, use the keywords "AND" and "OR" as required. Note that brackets can also be used to make logical groupings of conditions that must be met. For example, the following could be used to make data driven help available on a field on an Opportunity record:

IsPrivate = false OR (Type = 'Existing Customer - Downgrade' AND IsPrivate = true)

Help will only be shown for downgrades if the private box has been ticked.

One special case to bear in mind is that of new Salesforce records. When a User is adding an object:
  • A record will not have been created by the time the page is produced - so any data driven filter will fail (not be shown). However:
  • If the Author adds an Element with a blank filter, this will ALWAYS pass (see earlier entry in this Reading List), overriding any data driven filters when viewing or editing records. Therefore:
  • If data driven filters are desired, be sure to check the "Use for New Records" tick box against a particular Helped Element record to specify that it should be used for new records. This effectively ignores the data driven filter when creating a new record.

Note that you may only tick this box against one Helped Element for any given helpable within a "Visibility" context.

If the Helped Elements you expect to see do not appear for any reason:
  • On the affected Helped Page Layout, use Re-configure mode to see which DDF have been defined for a given element.
  • Note that on entry to Re-configure Mode, helpables with more than one associated element are highlighted with a number rather than just the usual help icon.
  • Edit the data driven filter(s) as required - or simply delete the Helped Element record(s) if they are no longer needed.
Note also the behaviour in Read Mode in cases where a Helped Element exists but its DDF does not match the Salesforce record being viewed:
  • If logged in as a Helped User, the affected element does not appear.
  • If logged in as a Help Author or Administrator, the affected element has special highlighting to show that Help exists but not for the current record. Clicking the element in these cases allows you to review the DDF that have been defined.

Data Driven Help is a feature of Improved Help that allows you to control the help that Users see based on the Salesforce record they are viewing. For example, you may wish to show different Help Topics depending on the Stage an Opportunity has reached or the Actual Cost of a Campaign.


This feature works by allowing Authors to create multiple Helped Element records for a given on-screen "helpable" (button, field, custom link etc) each with differing "Data-driven filter" values. Improved Help selects the Helped Element to use (and thus the associated Help Topic to display) by comparing these filters with the record the User is viewing; if the data does not "pass" the filtering criteria, it is not made available to the User.

Data driven filters can be based on multiple values in one or more fields by adding criteria together. To do this, use the keywords "AND" and "OR" as required. Note that brackets can also be used to make logical groupings of conditions that must be met. For example, the following could be used to make data driven help available on a field on an Opportunity record:

IsPrivate = false OR (Type = 'Existing Customer - Downgrade' AND IsPrivate = true)

Help will only be shown for downgrades if the private box has been ticked.

In general, there are few practical limits on the volumes of Helped Elements that can appear on a given Helped Page Layout: code has been "bulkified" wherever possible to ensure that provision of large amounts of help adds only trivial load to your Salesforce Org.

However, as at the present release of Improved Help, each Data Driven Filter present on a Layout will result in 1x SOQL query being generated (in order to test whether the current Salesforce record matches the specified criteria). Salesforce "governors" place limits on the number of such database operations allowed as a result of any single page request and these limits may vary from Org to Org. This makes it difficult for us to quote hard and fast limits as regards the volume of DDF that can be used on any given layout.

In general, we advise Customers to use DDF sparingly and, if help completely "disappears" (fails to be delivered) for a particular layout that has been successfully helped in the past, to consider the volume of DDF that may be in play and reduce this if required.

As Re-configure mode may not be available in these circumstances, we advise Help Administrators to use the Helped Page Layouts tab of the Improved Help App to locate, edit and/or delete the Helped Elements that may be breaking governor limits and thus causing help to cease to appear.
We love hearing from our Customers, so please do get in touch if we can be of assistance as you seek to tailor your help environment to local needs.

The following guidelines will help to ensure your use of the Bulk Upload Utility produces the results you expect:
  • Check version information: We add new fields and features to Improved Help on a regular basis, so please ensure you use the version of the Bulk Upload Utility that matches your Improved Help installation:
    • The Control Panel of the spreadsheet includes information about the version of Improved Help it serves.
    • Your Improved Help version can be checked by examining the Subscription tab of the Global Settings page.
  • Understanding record Ids: Most of the data entry tabs feature record Id columns. You may populate these with any alphanumeric identifiers you choose:
    • As record Ids are usually not maintained as data is moved from one Salesforce Org to the next, our utility does not attempt to retain the values you enter. The sole purpose of the Ids is to identify the relationships between your records: relationships (such as which Help Topics feature in which Reading Lists) will be replicated but the actual Ids used will not.
    • This means that if you are using data exported from Improved Help you may use record Ids "as is", but equally if you are creating fresh help records you may choose to use a simple numbering system, as we do in our Content Packs (examine the XML on which this Reading List is based for an example).
  • Paste with care: As a spreadsheet-based tool, the Bulk Upload utility readily allows copying and pasting of information. Be aware, however, that pasting in values will circumvent the data validation rules we've embedded into each sheet. If you do paste in bulk data, please make sure that it is of the correct type. For example, many cells are designed to accept only one of a set of pick list values: attempting to edit your pasted in values should reveal any data mis-matches.
  • Required Fields: The column headings of each tab are colour coded. Please note the meaning of these codings, as described on the sheets in question. For example, red field labels mean data must be entered into the columns concerned.
  • Text Validation: At present, our XML generator accepts only certain kinds of ASCII / basic text (it must be UTF-8 encoded): special characters, such as open / close quotes (“ ” as opposed to plain ") or the em-dash (– as opposed to the shorter minus sign -) cannot be accepted and will render the XML un-readable. Please use the blue "Text Validator" tab to check for these characters in your content and replace any "illegal" values with their web-encoded versions: this is usually as simple as swapping the offending character for the code number from the validator preceded by &# and followed by ; . For example, open quote (“) becomes “
  • Control panel functions: When you're ready, use the control panel to produce an upload-ready XML file. Be aware that the "Clear Contents" button, if used, will delete all the information you have entered and this action cannot be undone!

The Bulk upload utility is primarily intended for sharing and transporting relatively small quantities of help data between Orgs. It's ideal for individual Reading Lists or moderately sized packs of content.

Salesforce "governors" place limits on the number of database (SOQL) operations allowed as a result of any single page request. These limits may vary from Org to Org, as does the nature of the content entered using the Upload Utility.

This makes it difficult for us to quote hard and fast limits as regards the volume of data that can be uploaded via a single XML file. Whilst we have tested the upload of several hundred related records at once, we cannot predict the limits that may be encountered in individual Orgs.

In general, we advise Customers to split content into compact, manageable chunks where possible (this is also far easier in terms of maintenance).

Please be aware that our Export to Excel utility is an experimental feature of Improved Help version 1.21. Whilst we believe it to be robust in most circumstances, we cannot guarantee flawless operation.

Please further note that, as of this release, there is an upper limit of 1000 rows of data per object type in the export: if your Org contains, for example, more than 1000 Help Topics, exporting is likely to fail.

We recommend that Customers "prune" their help records where possible on a regular basis to remove unwanted or draft information.

We further recommend that most help creation be left to business experts "in situ", with bulk migration activities limited to scenarios envisaged for this toolset, as desribed elsewhere in this Reading List.

Don't forget that ALL of your Improved Help content takes the form of standard Salesforce records, so if our utilities cannot meet your needs, you're free to use any supported utility to export, manipulate and import help materials.

Improved Help's data input / output (I/O) utilities are designed to make it easier to package and transport help content between Orgs. The tools consist of:

  • The Documentation tab of the Global Settings page, where there is a facility to upload help content from Improved Help XML files;
  • A macro-enabled Excel (.XLSM) file known as the "Bulk Upload Utility" that produces XML in the required format based on help information typed onto spreadsheet tabs;
  • The Experimental Features tab of the Global Settings page which enables, among other things, bulk data Export to Excel in a format suited to use with the Bulk Upload Utility.

Please see associated reading lists and resources for more information.

Whilst all Improved Help data is stored in Salesforce and can therefore be manipulated and extracted using a variety of tools, we felt there was a need to offer a tailor made facility for creating related sets of help data and porting them from Org to Org.

We chose Extensible Mark-up Language (XML) as the vehicle for Improved Help I/O: we use a simple, informal, human readable schema to capture help records and their relationships.

The Documentation tab of the Global Settings page includes instructions on how to import help data by uploading files containing this XML: if you're viewing this information because you installed one of our optional "content packs", you'll be familiar with this process.

Production of XML files is covered later in this Reading List.

Version 1.21 of Improved Help saw the introduction of an "Experimental Features" tab to the Global Settings page. This controls access to certain product features, including export.

Note that Global Settings are only available to Help Administrators.

To export all your help records to an Excel format that is suited to the Bulk Upload Utility, please proceed as follows:
  • From the Quick Access Menu, select the Help Settings option.
  • On arrival at the Global Settings page, click the Experimental Features tab.
  • Ensure that the "Enable export of Help records to spreadsheet format" check box is ticked: if necessary, save this setting and refresh the Global Settings page.
  • Click the Documentation tab.
  • Click the "Export to Excel" link.
Clicking the link will initiate a download of help content. Note that:
  • The way the download proceeds and the resulting Excel file opens will vary depending on your browser and operating system;
  • The download may take some time to complete, depending on the volume of help data you have created;
  • On opening the file in Excel, you may or may not receive warnings about the format of the content: these can be ignored.

The Improved Help Bulk Upload Utility is ideal for helping with the following business needs:
  • You have legacy help content in external systems, particularly those that can be queried or where tabular export (CSV etc.) is offered, and you wish to import this material into Improved Help.
  • You have, or intend to produce multiple versions of the same content, perhaps in different languages or varying slightly according to the intended audience.
  • You wish to port help content from one Org to another (e.g., from a Sandbox to Production).
As an Excel-based tool, the Bulk Upload Utility makes it simple to replicate rows of help information then edit them as required en masse. One can also readily seed new help data from structured databases or files, such delimited or fixed width exports from third party systems.

This makes the Bulk Upload Utility the ideal tool to meet the kinds of business challenges described above.

The Bulk Upload Utility contains:
  • Yellow Tab: This is the "Control Panel" used to process that data on other tabs, where relevant.
  • Blue Tabs: These are additional utilities that can be used for checking your content. Information on these tabs is not processed into XML.
  • Green Tabs: These are for entry of your Improved Help data. There is one tab for each of the help objects the utility is able to process.
  • Red Tab: This tab (initially hidden) contains important lookup / validation information used by the remaining tabs. As a rule, you will not need to amend the contents of this tab.
Feel free to edit and/or extend any aspect of the spreadsheet, including our code, to meet local needs: spreadsheet tabs are protected, but you will find that neither the individual tabs nor the sheet as a whole are "locked" with passwords. The open nature of Excel and the potential complexity of multiple MS Office / operating system combinations are one of the reasons why we can only offer this tool "as is" and without warranties or guaranteed support levels.

We aim to provide Help to all your users, wherever they happen to be. For this reason, we've added internationalisation features that respond to your users' choice of language.

This brief Reading List explains how you can create your own localisations as and when you need them.

The Improved Help App ships with numerous custom Objects, Classes and Visualforce pages, each of which generate various on-screen labels and feedback messages. Our internationalisation features allow Orgs to provide their own translations for all of these elements ('translatables') by following a single, consistent, easy to use process:

  • Orgs can use our free, Excel-based translation tool (the 'Locale File Generator') to produce localisations.
  • Create one copy of the tool for each desired language. The tool contains a listing of all Help translatables and can be used to show where each is used within the App.
  • Each translatable appears in English, with an adjascent cell for the Org's desired translation.
  • Once all translations have been entered, the tool provides the means to produce Help-ready localisation XML (a 'Locale File').
  • Upload the Locale File to the Improved Help Documents folder, naming it according to the language it serves (see details later in this Reading List).
  • Help will seek translations in the Locale File appropriate to the logged in User's selected language: if no suitable file has been uploaded or particular translations are missing, default (English) values are used.

Internationalisation allows Orgs to provide their own, localised terminology (including overrides of our default English, if desired) for:

  • On-screen 'static' labels, such as those used in the Qucik Access Menu, the Help Portal and various dialogues;
  • Tool tips;
  • Feedback and diagnostic messages.

Note that internationalisation does not control help content, such as the text of Help Topics that are viewed. Content can be authored in any desired language and the appropriate Topics presented to Users using a variety of techniques, such as Data Driven Filters and/or Salesforce Data Sharing Rules.

Once all desired translations for a particular languge have been entered into the utility, click the 'Prepare XML' button on the 'Control Panel' tab to produce a localisation file.

Note that:

  • The tool will advise you to enter an XML file path if you have not done so, however the path is not checked for validity. Should you enter a non-existent path, the file may be produced at an unexpected location.
  • The tool will overwrite any file at the specified location without further warning.
Having produced the Locale file, upload it to the Improved Help Documents folder (as used for your Improved Help Subscription) in the destination Org: the file must be named [Language Code].xml, where [Language Code] is the combination of letters used by Salesforce to represent the language the file is to support. For example, for French, the file must be named fr.xml.

Uploaded internationalisation Locale files take effect for the relevant users immediately. It is therefore highly advisable to test them in a sandbox or similar prior to deployment in live situations.

To undo internationalisations, delete or rename the relevant Locale file.

• Certain translations are used in several Improved Help contexts. Try to ensure that your translations are suited to all of these.
  • Translation values may need to appear in limited screen real estate: try to match the brevity of the supplied English where possible.
  • If in doubt, use the 'Add diagnostic labels' option to gain an insight into where individual values are used.
  • Always test your translations before rolling them out in live situations.

The Locale File Generator is a standard, macro-enabled Excel spreadsheet (i.e., an XLSM file): ensure when opening your copy of the spreadsheet that you enable macros, otherwise it will not be possible to use the XML generation capabilities of the tool.

Orgs are free to examine the code underlying the tool and modify it as they see fit, however please bear in mind that it may be more difficult to offer support where modified versions of the tool are in use.

The tool consists of the following tabs:

Control Panel:
Provides an overview of how to use the tool, plus the 'Prepare XML' button that produces a Locale File at the specified path (enter the full path, including the desired file name and the .xml file extension).

Localisations:
Lists the translatables present in Improved Help. Orgs should fill in a translation for as many of these as desired in the 'Translation' column. Note that partially completed files may be used: the Prepare XML button will function as normal and the resulting Locale file can be uploaded so that non-blank translations for the relevant language will be adopted by Help. Where translations remain blank, Help will revert to using its default value for the affected translatable.

Branding:
If your Org has signed up for a "White Labelling" agreement with Improved Apps, this tab can be used to override the default "brandables", such as links to additional help and support. Where white labelling has not been arranged, this tab is ignored and default values are used throughout.

Each Localisation consists of the following columns:

  • #: The translatable's reference number. This can be used to help ascertain where each individual translation is used within Improved Help. When the 'Prepare XML' button is clicked, it will offer to add 'diagnostic markers' to each translation: enter 'Y' at this prompt to add the number from this column to each translation. On uploading the resulting XML file, translatable reference numbers will appear pre-pended to the locations where they are being used.
  • Context: This column provides a broad brush guide to where translations are used. This is generally the name of a Visualforce dialogue (as it appears in URLs) or an internal, functional reference: for example, 'Globals' are translations that are used throughout Improved Help.
  • Element Type: Provides an additional level of categorisation of the translation and its usage. For example, 'Message' translations tend to appear in prompts offered to Users, whereas 'Button' translations tend to be the text of a button or hyperlink presented within the specified Context.
  • Element: The reference name of the individual translation within its context. For example, for 'Field Label' Element Type translations, this will be the name of the individual field being translated. Whilst the value in the Element column is not necessarily unique, Context + Element Type + Element will be.
  • English: The default English version of this translatable.
  • Translation: The Org's desired translation of the translatable for the language covered by the copy of the Utility.
Note: before producing XML, ensure that Localisations remain sorted in ascending alphabetical order of Context, Element Type and Element.
